## Coverage and design basis

The requirements output defines REQ-001 through REQ-024. The solution design assigns TASK-001 through TASK-006 and has `coverage_dispositions: []`: no requirement is explicitly exempt. TASK-001 establishes the local Flask/synthetic foundation; TASK-002 implements pictured sign-in and revocable sessions; TASK-003 handles private recovery requests and quota; TASK-004 implements atomic single-use reset, session revocation and owner notification; TASK-005 supplies pytest; TASK-006 documents limits and audits the no-deployment constraint. Each test case must cite existing requirement and implementation-task IDs, concrete actions and observable expected outcomes; TASK-005 may additionally be linked for automated checks, not substituted for the behavioral task.

Design candidate TC-001 through TC-022 as future automated tests of REQ-001 through REQ-022, following the solution design's proposed verification matrix rather than claiming existing code or passing tests. Include both positive and negative/boundary checks: invalid sign-in/CSRF, known/unknown/throttled public-response parity with equivalent client context and no public link, five accepted known-account requests/suppressed sixth/new acceptance at the oldest +3600 seconds, usable unused token at 29:59/rejection at 30:00 from issuance, replay/concurrent submission, old/new password sign-in, all previously active independent sessions revoked, and exactly one owner-addressed in-memory success event per successful reset. Visual HTML/CSS assertions are not a claim of browser-rendered pixel fidelity. For REQ-023 and REQ-024, add explicit documentation/repository-and-work-record inspection cases (e.g., TC-023 and TC-024 linked to TASK-006), clearly identified as non-pytest verification; a purely automated-test claim for these would be misleading. The final traceability check should cover all 24 REQ IDs and all linked TASK IDs without using unsupported identifiers or exclusions.

## Assumptions, limits, open issues

- The design interprets the five-per-hour known-account quota as a rolling 3600-second window and treats tokens as invalid at or after 30 minutes; both boundary conventions are approved design assumptions, not additional words of the standard. No numeric quota for nonexistent accounts is specified.
- Only sign-in composition is pictured; reset/error/success/authenticated screens and their exact copy are proposals. Sink inspection is private to local tests or authorized same-process demonstration, never a public page or external delivery service.
- No runnable application or pytest suite is present in the reviewed repository; test cases will describe future verification, not record passing results or actual deployment activity. REQ-024's "no deployment performed" component needs delivery/work-record inspection, not an assertion that can be proved solely by source files.
- The approved predecessor outputs leave nonblocking questions about exact password policy, sign-in success UX, recovery/error copy, unknown-identifier accounting and private sink inspection procedure. Record these as assumptions or open questions in the later contract rather than inventing policy; escalate if a decision becomes necessary to specify an observable expected result.

Assessment only: no plan tasks, product JSON/Markdown or implementation changes were made in this phase.
